FACT_gate.statement: FACT: there exist n and A,B in Z_n with A+B=Z_n direct, {0,3,8,11} in A and {0,1,7,13,14} in B, all residues distinct.
FACT_gate.necessity: Every finite UD factor-complete superset M of C satisfies FACT with A = {0} union {s : a^s b^d in M} and B = {0} union {r : b^e a^r in M}. This is my written PR in shor-heterogeneous-completion-consolidated-v2.md section 2: LR+(1-z^n)H=S_n with nonnegative series forces a direct cyclic factorization. Equivalently it is the RSS89 theorem quoted by Cordero.
FACT_gate.consequence_for_assigned_quantifier: An actual PR-saturated prefix containing C has FACT data, and no such data is known in the literature or in my files (the earlier endpoint escapes were PR-incomplete). So the set quantified by 'EVERY PR-saturated actual finite prefix' is not known to be nonempty. A proof of not-FACT would block every terminating bridge and answer the Shor question negatively at the written PR interface. A FACT witness is the first necessary positive step. Either is existence-changing for this gate; neither is supplied yet.

new_written_results.R1_exact_reformulation: Named import: Sands 1979 Thm3, as quoted by Dai 2026 Thm2.2. A+B=Z_n is a factorization iff |A||B|=n and Div(A) and Div(B) meet only in {n}, where Div(E)={gcd(e-e',n)}. Therefore FACT is equivalent to a cardinality-plus-disjoint-gcd-division-set problem with the two containments.
new_written_results.R2_Sands_conjecture_failure: In any FACT solution, A is in no proper subgroup (3,8 in A, gcd(3,8)=1) and B is in none (1 in B). So FACT forces a counterexample to Sands' 1977/1979 conjecture, equivalently Tijdeman's conjecture mod n, as stated by Lagarias-Szabo 2001 section 2 and Dai 2026. Named imports: Sands 1979 proves the conjecture for n=p^a q^b, and Tijdeman proves it for good n. So FACT needs n with at least three distinct primes and not good. This is implied by 660|n, since 660 = p^2 q r s is not good, so it adds no new numerical restriction. Conversely, Szabo 1985, Lagarias-Szabo (n=900) and Dai 2026 (Szabo pairs for (pqr)^2) show such counterexamples exist. This route therefore yields NO contradiction.
new_written_results.R3_no_CRT_separable_solution: WRITTEN, using R1. Suppose Z_n = Z_n1 x Z_n2 with coprime n1,n2>1, and A=A1xA2, B=B1xB2 with Ai+Bi=Z_ni. One component, say n1, is prime to 3. There 0 and 3 are distinct in A1 with gcd(3,n1)=1, and 0 and 1 are distinct in B1 with gcd(1,n1)=1. So 1 lies in Div(A1) and Div(B1), contradicting R1 in Z_n1. Hence every FACT solution is genuinely non-product across any coprime CRT split. This is a route control: it excludes the product-of-factorizations construction class.
new_written_results.R4_size_four: WRITTEN. |A|=4 is impossible. Then A={0,3}+{0,8} is direct, so X=B+{0,8} is a complement of {0,3}. On every +3 orbit of Z_n, a complement of {0,3} takes alternate orbit positions. But X contains 0 and 9=1+8, which are three orbit steps apart (an odd distance). This is a reproof only: the earlier restricted result (a pure-end word a^l b^beta with l>=26 in every completion) already gives |A|>=5, hence |A|>=6.
new_written_results.R5_residue_invariance_tool: WRITTEN, from Tijdeman's multiplier theorem (named import, quoted by Dai 2026 from Coven-Meyerowitz). Let p|n be prime with p not dividing |A| or p^2|n. Then every t_k=1+k n/p is prime to |A|, so t_k A+B=Z_n. A character-sum argument over k in Z_p shows that each A^(r)+B is (n/p)-periodic, where A^(r)={a in A: a=r mod p}. So the residue of the A-component mod p is invariant under x -> x+n/p. The condition holds on the A side for p in {2,3,5,11} in every FACT solution. It is not yet used for a contradiction; it is recorded as a tool.
